Content and audience data for publishers and advertisers, San Mateo; Neustar bought it for $119M in 2013. The firm listed it in its 2008 portfolio, so the 2009-12 Form D band (Series A) cannot be the entry; the First Round book records the $20M Series B of April 2007 led by Kleiner Perkins after a 2005 seed, so the entry reads Growth (model, medium).

Home-sharing marketplace, San Francisco. Wikipedia: in June 2015 General Atlantic, Hillhouse, Tiger, Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and others invested $1.5 billion; the firm's own label reads Growth with a 2015 since-year, and KPCB Holdings appears on the 2020 S-1's registration rights. No earlier KP round is on record.

Group video chat from Sean Parker and Shawn Fanning, wound down after its relaunches (aligned with the a16z, GV and Sequoia rows; city New York as a16z and GV read it). Identity and physical-logical security convergence software, Fremont, California; still operating and privately held. Ray Lane was the KP director on the 2011 Form D.
Unified security management, San Mateo; AT&T bought it in 2018 (the firm's exit line: acquired by AT&T), aligned with the IVP row.

Edge-AI microcontrollers, Pleasanton (the firm's own description). Analog Devices announced an agreement to acquire Alif on 2026-09-09 with no price disclosed; the deal has not closed, so the row stays private below $1B.
Invisalign clear aligners; headquartered in Tempe, Arizona (Wikipedia).

Multi-cloud network as a service, San Jose. The firm's own post: 'We co-led the Series A in 2018' (with Sequoia; announced at the stealth exit in April 2020). Lumen completed the acquisition on 2026-07-07 (citybiz), aligned with the GV and Tiger Global rows.

Blockchain data platform (allium.so). The firm's post of 2024-07-18: 'having led their Seed round in 2022' and 'Today, Allium announced its Series A financing, with participation from Kleiner Perkins', so a Seed entry that graduated. The Wikidata country CZ is a one-word name match on another Allium and is replaced by US; the company's site names no city.

Seattle. The 1997 S-1's certain transactions: Series A Preferred Stock at $14.05 per share to Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VIII and KPCB Information Sciences Zaibatsu Fund II, with John Doerr a director since June 1996; the firm's own since-year is 1996.

AI clinical documentation, San Francisco. The firm's post of 2024-02-06: 'When we met Mike and Nikhil in 2020 and co-led their seed round' and now leads the Series B, so the entry is the 2020 Seed (the Form D band read the 2023 filing) and the named later round graduates it. Momentum check 2026-09-30: the $243M Series C at a $1.25B valuation (MedCity News, 2025-07-29) bands it 1b_plus.

Ultra-low-power chips, Austin (the 2025 S-1 cover). Wen Hsieh has been a director since November 2014; the S-1 names the KPCB entities' Series F-1 purchase but no source read names the round the firm entered.

Concentrated photovoltaic systems, headquartered in Seal Beach, California. After closing its Las Vegas plant it sold its assets to Arzon Solar, LLC in June 2014 (Wikipedia), which carried the CPV business on: acquired, an asset sale with a successor. The Green Growth Fund position sits in the $129.4M Series B that closed in April 2010.
Silicon-anode lithium-ion batteries, Fremont, California (NYSE: AMPX).

Synthetic biology (fuels, then ingredients), Emeryville. The 2010 S-1's certain transactions list 3,449,861 Series A preferred shares held by KPCB Holdings, as nominee; the Series A was sold in April and May 2007 at $2.174 (John Doerr a director since May 2006, the firm's 2006 year). So the entry is the Series A, not the Seed band read off a 2008 Form D. Chapter 11 in 2023; status as pre-filled.

Online services and media; headquartered in New York since 2007, sold by Yahoo to Bending Spoons in 2026 (Wikipedia). The firm's case study: 'invested in AOL in September 1987' (Frank Caufield had earlier led the investment in Control Video Corp., AOL's predecessor); no round is named.

Application security posture management, Tel Aviv (as the Greylock and General Catalyst rows). The firm's post of 2020-10-13: 'We're excited to co-lead apiiro's Series A' with Greylock; it was the company's first round at its stealth exit. General Catalyst led the $100M Series B in 2022; no $1B+ priced round on record.

Application performance monitoring, San Francisco; Cisco bought it for $3.7B in January 2017, days before its IPO. The S-1 has KP's shares held by KPCB XIV and the KPCB Digital Growth Fund; model: the firm first came in on the 2011 Series C (the firm's since-year 2011, after the 2008 A and 2010 B by Greylock and Lightspeed), a Growth entry.

Vehicle and physical-AI software. The firm's own post of 2025-06-17: 'We first invested six years ago at the Series B' (the $40M Lux-led round of 2019), so the site's 2018 year is not the entry. The pre-filled $1.25B (2020) mark is stale: the $600M Series F and tender co-led by BlackRock and Kleiner Perkins valued it at $15B (the company's release), aligned with the Coatue, General Catalyst and Lux rows. The firm's live description places the headquarters in Sunnyvale (the sibling rows still read Mountain View).

Saltwater stationary batteries, Pittsburgh. It filed for Chapter 11 in March 2017 and its assets were sold at auction (Wikipedia): acquired, an asset sale out of insolvency. Kleiner Perkins is named among its investors, but no source read names the round the firm first joined.

Interactive product demo software, San Francisco. The firm's post of 2024-11-21: 'We're excited to lead Arcade's Series A'; the earlier 2021-22 filings are seed money before the firm. Outside the momentum sectors; no $1B+ round on record.

Security information and event management, Cupertino; IPO 2008, bought by HP in 2010. Ted Schlein has been a director since March 2002 (the 2007 S-1) and the firm's since-year is 2002; no source read names the round.
Anti-phishing email security, Redwood City; Cloudflare bought it for $162M in April 2022 (Wikipedia).

Chemistry instruments and consumables for drug discovery, Foster City; IPO 2000, bought by Biotage in 2005 (as the IVP row). Brook Byers chaired it from 1995 (the 2001 10-K) and KP funds filed 13Gs from 2001; no round is named.

Immuno-oncology (pegilodecakin), Redwood City; Eli Lilly bought it for about $1.6B in 2018. The S-1's certain transactions show entities affiliated with Kleiner Perkins buying $7.9M of the Series B (2014), then B-1, C and C-1; no earlier KP preferred series is listed and the firm's since-year is 2014, so Growth (medium: Beth Seidenberg sat on the board from December 2012).

Antibodies against extracellular-matrix targets for cancer and fibrosis, Palo Alto (the firm's 2008-11 listing); Gilead bought it (the firm's exit line). The firm's since-year is 2007; no source read names the round.

Programmable T-cell therapies, headquartered in South San Francisco (the company's 2024 release, which names Kleiner Perkins among existing investors in the $325M Series C, no valuation disclosed). Model: the firm co-founded it in the $85M Series A of 2019 (the firm's since-year).
Remote-access networking, Alameda; IPO 1994, bought by Lucent in 1999. Wikipedia names KPCB, Greylock and NEA as initial investors without a round name, as the Greylock, Menlo and NEA rows read it.

Allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy (the atara-bio row is the same company). Headquarters now in Thousand Oaks, California.
Audiobooks and spoken audio, headquartered in Newark, New Jersey (Wikipedia); IPO 1999, bought by Amazon in 2008. KP funds filed 13Gs in 2000-01 and the firm's since-year is 1998; no round named.

Decentralised music streaming, San Francisco. The firm's since-year is 2018, the year of the Series A the Lightspeed card names; no source read ties Kleiner Perkins to a named round (the General Catalyst row is undetermined too).

Compact linear Fresnel solar thermal, Mountain View; Areva bought it in 2010 (as the Khosla row). The firm listed it in 2008, before the 2009-04 Form D on file, so that date is a later round; no source read names the round KP first joined.

Implantable sphenopalatine-ganglion stimulator for cluster headache, Redwood City (the firm's 2008-11 listing). Its domain ati-spg.com now redirects to Realeve, which markets the same Pulsante system (checked 2026-09-30), so the business continues under a successor: acquired, medium confidence.

Auxogyn merged with Fertility Authority and renamed itself Progyny (Nasdaq: PGNY), headquartered in New York; market cap $1.93B on 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis), as pre-filled. KPCB XIII's Form 3 at the 2019 IPO reports Series A and Series B preferred; with Beth Seidenberg a director on the $18M Form D of 2012, the entry is the Series A (medium).

Real-time location systems for hospitals, San Diego. Its last Form D is from 2017 and its own website no longer serves (expired certificate, checked 2026-09-30); no acquisition or shutdown found, so the state is unknown.
